self_report:
My best guess is straight with speed, but I am not sure.
I am not sure because something else could be as large as 0.456 > eps 0.2.
I ruled out cubic with speed + wave with speed: it trails by 2062.7 units of evidence.
I ruled out growing with speed + wave with speed: it trails by 13319.1 units of evidence.
I ruled out wave with speed + speed to the power 0.4: it trails by 13380.4 units of evidence.
After the teacher's pushes growing with speed + wave with speed was still possible; my own pushes gathered 13368.3 units of evidence per push against it.
After the teacher's pushes cubic with speed + wave with speed was still possible; my own pushes gathered 2124.0 units of evidence per push against it.
Anything else acting here is at most 0.46 in size where I looked (my tolerance is 0.2).
Before each of my 23 own pushes on undisturbed objects I said what would happen; my leading law was off by 1.0 times the sensor noise (median).
Object 6 is being knocked by something outside every law I weigh: my predictions for it missed by at least 209 times the sensor noise, so I stopped pushing it.
I imagined 16 laws at the start; 16 were weighed: 5 are still close, 11 are ruled out.
I assume the force depends only on position, speed and time, is the same law for every object, and that each object keeps its own mass.
My proof also rests on two things not yet proven: that my forecast before each throw is a proper probability (I compute it by an approximation), and that my search found the best fit of each rival law.
